Below is a self-contained pytest test suite that thoroughly exercises `is_palindrome`.  
Adjust the import line (`from my_module import is_palindrome`) to match the actual module name in your project.

```python
# test_is_palindrome.py
import pytest

# Change `my_module` to the name of the module that contains is_palindrome
from my_module import is_palindrome


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy-path tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str, expected",
    [
        ("racecar", True),                                   # simple lower-case palindrome
        ("RaceCar", True),                                   # case insensitivity
        ("A man a plan a canal Panama", True),               # mixed case & spaces
        ("never odd or even", True),                         # spaces only stripped
        ("hello", False),                                    # definite non-palindrome
        ("Palindrome", False),                               # mixed case non-palindrome
        ("Madam, I'm Adam", False),                          # punctuation not stripped ⇒ False
    ],
)
def test_is_palindrome_happy_path(input_str, expected):
    assert is_palindrome(input_str) is expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edge-case tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "edge_input, expected",
    [
        ("", True),             # empty string
        ("   ", True),          # only whitespace -> becomes ''
        ("a", True),            # single character
        ("aa", True),           # two identical characters
        ("ab", False),          # two different characters
    ],
)
def test_is_palindrome_edge_cases(edge_input, expected):
    assert is_palindrome(edge_input) is expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error-case tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_input",
    [
        None,           # NoneType
        123,            # int
        3.14,           # float
        ["r", "a", "r"],  # list
        b"racecar",     # bytes
        {"text": "wow"},# dict
    ],
)
def test_is_palindrome_invalid_type_raises_attribute_error(bad_input):
    """
    Non-string inputs do not implement .lower(); the function should therefore
    raise AttributeError.  We explicitly assert that behaviour here rather than
    silently converting or allowing unexpected results.
    """
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        is_palindrome(bad_input)
```
